page: The OVHcloud b3-640 is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated AMD EPYC hardware. It provides 160 physical cores and 160 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration pairs these dedicated compute cores with 640 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provisioned via an integrated 400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps. It contains no discrete graphics accelerators and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance testing shows high scaling across highly parallelized tasks. The 160 dedicated cores achieve top-decile results in multi-core compute metrics, including stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation benchmarks. Cached memory throughput ranks in the top ten percent, supporting extreme transactional loads such as Redis SET operations exceeding 170 million operations per second. However, single-threaded execution is moderate, with Geekbench single-core scores falling within the middle fifty percent of evaluated systems due to the 2.3 GHz clock frequency. Furthermore, while prompt processing throughput for large language models remains viable, raw text generation speeds for 70B parameter models drop significantly without dedicated GPU acceleration.

With its balanced memory allocation, dedicated core density, and fast NVMe storage, the b3-640 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for massive multi-threaded enterprise workloads. The hardware profile fits distributed caching systems, large-scale software compilation pipelines, parallel data processing, backend microservice clusters, and high-throughput static web hosting where multi-core scaling takes precedence over peak single-core clock frequencies.
description: The OVHcloud b3-640 is a dedicated general-purpose instance featuring 160 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 640 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute and decompression performance, alongside high cached memory bandwidth capable of supporting over 170 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance consistent with its 2.3 GHz base frequency, and large language model generation suffers due to the absence of hardware accelerators. The b3-640 provides robust resource density for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, enterprise database caching, and high-concurrency web serving workloads.
